title: Vanderbilt BIEN Lab SOZ Resting State SEEG Classification (processed resting-state SEEG)
description: Processed resting-state stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from 79 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy evaluated at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Each patient contributed five minutes of awake, eyes-closed, interictal data in a bipolar montage, filtered and labeled with region-level seizure onset zone (SOZ) ground truth. The data support training and analysis of deep neural networks that classify SOZ versus non-SOZ brain regions.
methods_description: Five minutes of awake, eyes-closed interictal resting-state SEEG were recorded per patient at sampling rates of 500-2048 Hz. Signals were converted to a bipolar montage of adjacent contacts and filtered with MATLAB filtfilt Butterworth passbands (1-59, 61-119, 121-150 Hz). Contacts were localized on post-implantation CT with CRAVE and assigned to Desikan-Killiany regions. SOZs were defined per region as those containing any contact involved in ictal onset.
